patch_description:
Replace the final “single worst triangle” axis-aligned polish with an active-constraint directional search. In a maximin Heilbronn configuration, several nearly minimal determinants are normally simultaneously tight, so improving only the arbitrarily selected minimum triple often traps the search by worsening another almost-active triple.

The new refinement collects all triples within a small tolerance of the current lower tail, visits every movable point participating in them, and tests a deterministic stencil. Besides simplex-coordinate directions, the stencil includes directions toward and away from the centroid of each active triangle’s other two vertices. These partner-centroid directions directly alter the restrictive determinant and are substantially better aligned with the nonsmooth maximin geometry than axis steps. Candidate acceptance is lexicographic: first improve the exact minimum, then improve the mean of the lower tail when the minimum is tied. This preserves the primary objective while resolving degeneracies and preparing further minimum increases.
